 How busy will DTW be this holiday season? Airport expects 4 million travelers
 1.6 million passengers are expected to travel at DTW for Christmas and New Year’s
 Samantha Sayles , Senior Digital Producer
 Published:  November 20, 2026 at 5:00 AM Tags:  Detroit Metro Airport , Romulus , Wayne County A passenger walks through McNamara terminal past a Delta aircraft at Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport in Detroit, Thursday, Jan. 14, 2010. (Paul Sancya, (AP Photo/Paul Sancya)) More than 4 million travelers are expected to pass through Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport this holiday season, the Wayne County Airport Authority said Thursday.
 From Nov. 20 through Nov. 29, more than 900,000 passengers are expected to travel for the Thanksgiving holiday.
 Recommended Videos
 From Dec. 18 through Jan. 3, more than 1.6 million passengers are expected to travel for Christmas and New Year’s.
 DTW expects more than 4 million passengers traveling between Nov. 20 and Jan. 3.
 “We anticipated a slight dip in traffic this holiday season following Spirit Airlines’ sudden shutdown, but our commitment to delivering a world-class experience hasn’t wavered,” said WCAA CEO Chad Newton. “The entire DTW team is working hard to take the stress out of travel, so our customers can focus on shopping, dining and relaxing before they fly.”
 DTW provided the following traveling tips to passengers:
 Arriving early makes it easier for everyone. During the holiday season, the airport experiences an increased number of infrequent travelers who may require additional time. To ensure a smooth and stress-free experience, you are advised to arrive early. The airport recommends arriving at least two hours prior to a domestic flight and three hours prior to an international flight. Allocating enough time will allow for parking, baggage check-in, Transportation Security Administration (TSA) screening, and reaching the departure gate without rushing. 
 Check your bags for prohibited items before arriving at DTW. Attempting to pass through TSA screening with prohibited items in your baggage may result in delays for both you and other passengers. For information on prohibited items, visit tsa.gov/travel/travel-tips. Please note prohibited items are not only weapons, but also include liquids and gels exceeding 3.4 ounces. 
 Bring your REAL ID-compliant driver’s license or state-issued ID. If you do not possess a REAL ID, you may use a valid passport, military ID, or another form of identification accepted by the TSA. Without one of these forms of identification, you may be denied access through the security checkpoint or subjected to additional screening. Travelers without an acceptable ID can pay a $45 fee to use TSA ConfirmID for a 10-day travel period. Identity verification is not guaranteed. 
 Avoid wrapping gifts prior to traveling. Packages that are sealed may be subject to inspection by TSA, potentially resulting in delays and inconvenience at screening checkpoints. 
 Arrange for assistance in advance. The Airport Authority and its partners are dedicated to ensuring a welcoming and seamless travel experience for all passengers. Travelers requiring additional assistance are encouraged to notify their airline or the TSA in advance. Additional information is available at metroairport.com or by contacting TSA Cares at 855.787.2227.
